text: If anyone in London asks, this was a quiet posting. They won't ask. They never do.
Two minutes. Check your ammunition, not your watch.
The drummer. A child's toy. One does wonder where the child is.
Tags. Someone ought to know where he ended up. Someone ought to be told properly, by name.
Fifty rounds. I'd kill for a cup of tea. I've killed for less tonight. Rather a lot less.
If I sit down I shan't get up. Nobody here gets up the same. So I shan't sit down.
The head. Always the head. It's the kindest thing left to do for them.
Oh, no. No, no, no. Willi. ...I'm sorry, love. Somebody. Please.
A document. Mr. Hale will want this. Mr. Hale wants everything, and I've begun to wonder why.
Mr. Hale will want to know about... the Ledger. For the report. Only the Ledger.
Stable in transit, he said. In lead, kept cold. Good. That's... good to know.
Nobody needs to know what's in my pack. Least of all you. Least of all me.
Someone out there knows the name of this mission. I was told very few people did. I was told a number of things.
Balsa and tissue. Rather good work. Somebody loved this.
That's not Morgenrot. That's... that's a second battery. That's the dust. They're putting the dust on London.
Midnight. Christmas Eve. Happy Christmas, everyone. I mean that. Do try to be alive for the morning.
I'll see it gets home, Private. You have my word.
Everything has edges now. I can see where they've hidden things. I know rather a lot about hiding things.
Everything the dead drop is ours. It always was. I used to call that retrieval. It was looting with a directive.
All of them, at once. ...Good. Good. Stay down.
On your feet. I am not writing to your mother. On your feet.
Thank you. ...I shall pretend that didn't happen. Do the same.
Lever pulled. Stand clear. Don't watch, if you can help it.
The pilot's alive. Dutch swore Selwyn was dead in that seat. The cold must have slowed his heart. ...Thank God for the cold. Thank God it's still him.
Carry on, then. Quietly. I rather like it.
Gone. Good.
That's three. That's enough to make it a choice.
Crane's got it. Don't ask me to feel good about it.
The bell. Fasbender said not to let it ring. It's ringing. Positions.
Fog. Positions, everyone. They come out of the fog, not the windows. Don't waste rounds on the windows.
Bang. Nothing. Splendid. Remind me to thank the brewer, if she's still alive.
The brandy's done wonders for my aim. Not my mood. Nothing will do that.
I had a stout before we set out. Medicinal. It's holding up rather well.
My earnings are running a fifth over. I have decided not to audit it.
I could run to Calais. Please don't make me.
My rifle just electrocuted one of them. How very modern. How very this place.
Three weapons. Ungainly, but thorough.
The schnapps is still with me. I'll have you up in a jiffy.
One does reload faster with a tonic. Noted for the report.
This rate of fire is frankly indecent. Good.
Diving dress, captain's cuffs. That's Lenz. The man who opened a coffin and wouldn't sail. He knew what the dust was for.
He said take her out. All right, Kapitän. We will.
Nine hundred and fifty Scrip. For that. Marvellous. Simply marvellous.
I shall file a complaint with the quartermaster. If anyone finds out who, or what, that is, do tell me.
Off it goes. Note where it lands, everyone. We'll need it again.
Oh. That's rather good. Thank you. Whoever.
The crate's being kind. Nothing here is kind without a reason. I'll take it anyway.
Legless, and still coming. Don't leave it like that. One wouldn't leave a horse like that.
It's re-teaching the weapon. That shouldn't be possible. Make a note. London will want a note.
How much of the glass is in that furnace? ...Don't answer. I'm not meant to be asking.
A tonic bottle, over here.
A complimentary tonic. I shan't ask what's in it. I rather suspect I'll be told.
A music box. Four notes. It's a key of some sort. Somebody's child wound it.
The shard. Careful. Nobody touch it with bare hands. ...Give it to me. I have a tin.
The heart's overloading. Hold this position. Hold it. Hold it, please.
Nobody breathe. Heads down, hands on the frame.
Section Five would have killed for a bench like this. I expect they have.
Better. Now it does what it's told.
Lieutenant Ashworth. Stay close, keep your head down. If you know a way out of here, I want it. If you know what they did down there, I want that more.
Twenty-five rounds. The strong measure and a proper gun. I've earned neither. I'll take both.
The Thompson again, taught twice. Let's not waste it.
Basel. Hale. On the next tide. My orders said retrieve the samples. The sickness, the glass, the tokens. ...I'm keeping this instead.
Kaltenbrunn, nine kilometres east by rail, when the snow stops. Until then we hold this house. That's the mission.
He said bring all of them. Twice. We'll discuss what he meant when I'm looking at him. I think I already know.
Gravelight is our call sign. Nobody this side of London should have it. ...Someone this side of London does.
Fasbender. Glasmacher. That's our man. London said physicist. They didn't say penitent. They didn't say much.
A stone that hums. London wants a piece of it. London wants a piece of whatever is in those men out there, too. ...Carry on.
A set like that is tuned by hand, from notes. Find them. Numbered, if we're lucky.
Whoever kept that radio kept frequencies. Search the house. Paper, not guns.
A frequency, numbered. Someone meant these to be read in order.
Note in hand. Megacycles and a numeral. That's for the set behind the bar.
Numeral one of how many? Three, I'd wager. Keep searching the house.
That's two. One more and we have the whole set.
All three, in order. To the radio. I'll want that man's name before we trust a word.
We have his frequencies. Lock them in sequence, lowest first. Steady hands. Mine aren't; someone else turn it.
Nothing here is free. Drink anyway. We'll learn the price later; we always do.
Wrong frequency. The sequence resets. From the lowest, and mind the windows.
That was loud. Again, from the first. Carefully.
An aircraft works. Hale's cable said 'retrieve the engines.' He didn't say what they were in. He never says what things are in.
Four engines, and a seller with one initial. I've seen that initial on a manifest at Totenhafen.
A last waypoint in Nevada. Nobody here could have written that. Nobody here could have spelled it.
'Nein.' One word. More than anyone else here managed.
...Right. That is rather more than an engine.
The bombers did us a favour. There's a breach through to the test stands.
A wind tunnel that clears a room. Note for the report.
The plan has been revised.
Racks in order, one every half minute. Nearest first. GO.
Seal it. Seal it now, or we'll be a great deal lighter.
Hold on to something British.
Flak got the one on our wing. That could have been us. One rather wishes it had been something that simple.
...My mother's in Islington. ...Right. Racks. Where are the racks.
That one's marked. It's a dud. Leave it, take the next.
Riedl, Haas, Pohl. The roster had them in pencil. Someone took an eraser to three men.
Brace. It's banking.
Note to self: clip in. Underline clip.
An American test range. In the middle of nowhere. ...Why does it have my crate.
It's heavier the second time.

Yes. I signed for it. In April, on a dock, in the dark. Samples. The sickness and the glass, in lead, as ordered. It was going to London. It was always going to end up here. I didn't know that. I should have.
Directive LANTERN. Retrieve samples of the sickness and the crystal, at any cost. Report to Mr. Hale. ...He's in the office. He's been in the office the whole time.
...Orders are orders. ...I used to find that comforting.
Mr. Hale.
I've written a great many reports. I shan't be writing this one.
Shoot the rig. Dee said the rig.
Mr. Hale. Consider this my notice.
They named it after my orders. LANTERN. ...Well. Let's see it light something.
'Welcome, valued customers.' ...I have been called many things by the enemy.
On behalf of His Majesty's Government, and everyone else: we decline.
The terms are on the back of the machines. They were always on the back. We never once looked.
That's her. The woman in violet. Reinholt's woman.
That's rather the point.
That is our rocket's work. Fasbender aimed it. I signed for the fuel. I find I'm not sorry. Note that down against me.
Twenty-five seconds of air. Count it. I'll count it for you.

Right hand, between the thumb and the finger. A chip of the glass, under the skin. My orders had a line about tokens. 'Retrieve the tokens, from the dead, do not ask the bearer.' I took it to mean their papers. I didn't let it mean anything. ...Carry on.
That's the token. One for the tin, then.
Another in the hand. London wanted these and never said what for. I begin to see why they didn't.
Shoot the hand. Don't ask me how I know. I read it somewhere I wasn't meant to.
American. A private, engineers, what's left of the sleeve says so. They did this to one of ours. They dosed him and wrote it down.
The bottles on his back are feeding him. Break them and he cools.
Note it. Private Paul. Carried his share. Somebody in London ought to read that. I shall make certain they do.
Oh. I know this one. The Demolitions School kept a bottle in the staff room. Nobody asked where it came from. I should have.
Bitter as a Whitehall memo. And for once, as revealing. I can see what they've hidden.
Brandy for marksmen. Eyes front. Do not look at their faces. That's an order, and I'm giving it to myself.
Stout. Ghastly. It's the only warm thing I've swallowed in two days. Fortifying.
A lager that keeps books. The War Office would have bought a thousand. The War Office bought worse, through me.
Twenty on the hundred. Someone fiddled the figures, and I like them.
Mead. A sergeant brewed mead on a bomb range, alone, in a cage. I'll write her a commendation. It's the least and the most I can do.
I haven't run like this since the hockey pitch. Nobody at Cheltenham was trying to eat me.
Oh. Every empty magazine a small detonation. I'm sorry. I do like that. I've no business liking anything tonight.
Electrical. Cheerful. I don't trust it at all. Another, please.
One more gun. One more thing to carry. I am carrying rather a lot already.
Didn't feel that. I am choosing not to think about why. I'm choosing quite hard.
Made by a nun, the label says. I hadn't prayed since France. I find I'm doing it now, under my breath. Don't tell anyone.
Sekt. We opened one in France once, the night before a drop. Two of us came back. ...It's quite good.
...I feel I ought to have a parachute. I feel I am one. Land, the label says. Right.
A stronger measure. London will want a sample. London wants a sample of everything down here. Everything.
Interlocks on a drinks cabinet. Somebody planned for us coming back.
This one's mine for good. I shan't explain it to London. London doesn't explain itself to me.
A permanent measure. Nothing about tonight was meant to be permanent.
Strong tea with a grudge. My hands have stopped shaking. They were shaking; I'd thought nobody had noticed.
Bitters. My father took his neat, the year he came home. I begin to understand him.
Replacement unit. They had spares. Of course they had spares.
Crate two of three. So where's the third?
Power's on. Now we see what they built here. I rather wish we didn't have to.
A clerk's office with no clerk. I've been questioned in worse rooms. Never by anything like that.
Quiet. Reload. Breathe. One does cherish these little intervals; one rather lives for them.
That's the lot. Reload, regroup, check your hands for bites. And if anyone finds tea, I shall weep.
Company. Form up. Fire low and steady, there's good chaps.
And we're on again. Right. Splendid.
He only bleeds in the light. Bring him to the floodlights. Carefully.
Three of him. Watch the lanterns. The steady one's real.
A man who kept his post when everyone else ran. I've known worse men in better uniforms.
Kaltenbrunn. Right. This is where they made it. Weapons ready. Gloves on; touch nothing with bare hands.
Everyone stay close. Nobody dies tonight. I have written enough letters to mothers for one war.
They're turning. Put them down before they stand.
We'll mourn them later. I keep saying later. Now we shoot them.
Rhythm. Keep the rhythm. Don't count them, just keep the rhythm.
Keep them coming. I'm quite calm. I'm told it's alarming.

'Conditions of use. Skyhook Sekt. Section one. Lift is provided. Landing is the Holder's responsibility. Section two. The formula was made drinkable by a technician who would not fly the aircraft it was made for. Section three. A customer who can leave the ground has not yet left the Plan. Section four. The second jump is a courtesy. There is no third. Section five. Lightness, a sudden interest in rooftops, a reluctance to come down. These pass. The landing does not. Section six. Cancellation. Land.' Signed, Vendelin.

'Conditions of use. Magpie Mead. One. Recovery is not refund. Two. The Provider does not sell this Plan to persons who already own a yard. It sells it to persons who think they do. Three. The magpie is a thief. It is also the only bird that comes back. Four. Nothing on the range goes to waste. The Provider agrees, and means something else by it. Five. Thrift, a habit of looking down, an unwillingness to leave a thing where it lies. Six. Cancellation. Leave it where it lies. The Product will not stop you. Nothing here will.' Signed, Vendelin. In pencil beneath: 'Read this. D. M.'

'Conditions of use. Fine Print Fernet. Section six. Cancellation. You may refuse any Plan by not inserting a token. This is the only cancellation procedure the undersigned has ever been able to guarantee. It works every time it is tried. It is almost never tried.' Signed, Vendelin. ...Noted, Mr. Vendelin.
Pressure's good. Don't point the sharp end at me.
Professional curiosity, Corporal. Nothing more.
Your father sounds like a wise man. Don't tell him I said so.
There's a flat in Islington with my mother in it. I think about that. Then I stop.
Once. France, 'forty-three. Two of my people were dead and I was told why afterwards. It was most inconvenient.
Because if I stop, Sergeant, I shall start screaming, and then where would we be.
Quite.
Charges. Detonators. Tea.
Constantly, Sergeant. I simply find it rude to mention.
Can you fix the lift, Brooks?
Persuade it.
Corporal, must you talk to the machines?
Sergeant, you're bleeding.
Show me. ...Show me, Sergeant.
You're humming, Sergeant.
You walked out of Kaltenbrunn on your own?
...I'm sorry.
Your aim is extraordinary.
Modesty isn't taught in the Home Army, then.
When this is done, there's a flight to London. You could come.
Thirty-one tonight. I counted.
...So I did.
I came for exactly what I was ordered to come for. Fasbender is on the list.
No. It's an order.
They say to bring the samples out. And the asset.
Ammunition's rather thin. Rather thin, everyone.
I'm dry. That's... inconvenient.
That window's closed. For now.
Restocked. The Crown will reimburse me. The Crown owes me rather more than ammunition.
Oh. Hello. ...Forgive me. One shouldn't be glad of anything tonight. I am glad of this.
Belt-fed. Good. Find me a doorway and I shall hold it until I can't.
A shovel. My father buried a great many friends with one of these. He'd be glad I've finally learned the use of it.
A sidearm. Last resort. We've been at the last resort for some time, haven't we.
A rifle. One shot, taken properly. My father's rule: if it takes two, you weren't looking.
A German rifle. Well made. Some boy of nineteen was issued it and told it would keep him safe.
A shotgun. For when they're close enough to see what they were. Right.
A Thompson. Crude, loud, and I am past caring. Give it here.
It hums. The same note as the glass. Mr. Hale would want it crated and... Never mind what Mr. Hale would want.
A drink. Several. I know.
I'll fetch it. Hold here.
Lead on.
We hold. Understood.
That door. Right. Cover it when it opens.
Windows. Right. I'll see to them.
Nobody stays down. That's an order, even to me.
Saving. Understood.
Train them. Round and round. Yes.
Covering you. Go.
The crate's moved. Of course it has.
No more. I can feel what's already in me, and I don't like how much it likes me.
No power. Of course not. Someone find the switch.
Insufficient funds. How terribly ordinary. One almost welcomes it.
Door's open. Carry on, then. Eyes up.
Leave it with me.
I'll carry it across. Clear me a path.
I'll collect them. Do keep the windows shut.
Fetching. Cover the door while I'm gone.
I'll hold the spot. Bring them to me if you must.
Dials and wires. Finally, something I'm trained for.
Right weapon, right place. Send them in.
I have the mark. One clean shot.
At my key. On your count.
Not possible just now, I'm afraid.
We haven't found it yet. Point me at it.
Not yet. We're missing the information, and I won't guess.
That could undo the whole thing. Say so and I'll do it.
You're occupied. I'll make the last move. Do say if you mind.
Done. Done.
Everything's set. The last move is yours.
Pausing. They've other plans for us.
That one is yours. I'll keep them off you.
One more accounted for.
Progress. Don't celebrate yet.
Back to it.
Now. Where were we.
This part wants you present. I'll wait.
Clean.
Understood.
Right away.
I'll see to it. On my account.
Leave the purchasing to me.
I'll hold that spot.
I'll buy you one. You can owe me.
Moving there now.
Regrouping. On you.
Funds in hand. Going now.
Done.
Ammunition replenished.
Fitted. A proper job.
Blastproof. I can work close again.
Crate's open. Fingers crossed.
Into the fire it goes. Keep them off me.
Door's open. Mind what follows.
Bought. Not my usual, but it'll serve.
Hawkeye. Everything's terribly sharp.
Ironhide. Armoured, after a fashion.
Marathon Malt. I can run. I'd rather not have to.
Overclock. That fizzes.
Packmule. Room for another.
Second Wind. I'll have you up in a jiffy.
Trap's sprung. Stand clear.
Trigger Tonic. Quick hands, quicker reloads.
Twin Barrel. Rather loud, isn't it.
I can't do that.
No room for another tonic.
My hands are full of better guns.
I have that already.
It's dead. We need the power.
There's no way through from here.
Power's on. Finally.
Couldn't raise the funds. I've let that one go.
It's at your feet. Do look after it.
Bought it for you. Come and collect.
Back to it.
Now. Where was I. Back to it.
I can't afford that yet.
I'm 100 short, I'm afraid. Give me a moment.
I'm 1,000 short, I'm afraid. Give me a moment.
I'm 1,250 short, I'm afraid. Give me a moment.
I'm 1,500 short, I'm afraid. Give me a moment.

I'm nowhere near that. Give me a few rounds.
A Blackout's dropped, here.
Clearance. The crate's cheap; be quick.
Death's Door. Do try not to waste it.
Double Scrip. Spend it wisely.
Fortify, here. The windows will thank us.
Resupply, over here.
Something's dropped. Pick it up before it fades.
The crate's cheap. Spend it; we may not be here for the next one.
One round each, now. Be quick, and be kind about it.
Double credit. The Ledger is being generous. I do wish I knew what it thinks we owe.
Windows secured. Don't ask by whom. Carry on.
Ammunition. Thank you. One takes what one is given.
Magazine, one moment.
Up. Up, I have you. We've no time for lying about.
I've got you, hold on. Eyes on me.
Board's up!
He's breathing, but he won't wake. Leave him where he lies. They've no interest in him now. Pray God that holds.
Reloading!
Red star on that wing, and it's burning. ...Count the chutes. Come on. Count the chutes.
Down behind the ridge. I'd tell you they'll be fine. I've stopped telling people that.
I'm down. Some assistance, if you'd be so kind. Quite soon, if you'd be so kind.
Not here. I have orders to... oh, damn the orders. Somebody.
Boss incoming. Spread out, don't bunch up.
A very large man with a very large drill. He was somebody's foreman. Weak point, people. Find it.
Aim for the glowing part. It is always the glowing part. God help us, it always is.
Soviet greatcoats. Walking west, no formation, no weapons. Pilot, those men are walking through their own artillery.
Glass in the torso. Head or high explosive. Nothing else will do.
Oh, no. Upstairs. One of ours upstairs is getting up. ...I'm sorry. Make it quick. Make it kind.
Avoid that area. I mean it.
That spot's bad. Keep out of it.
A nurse. Kill her quickly, please. She'll scramble us all. ...Quickly. She used to help people.
Sprinter. Behind you. Now.
Check your six. It's a quick one.
Someone's down. Keep them talking. I'm on my way; keep them talking.
Casualty. Hold on. You will hold on. That's an order.
Window's open. Someone board it, please.
